question.text: A trader sells 10 lots of USDINR futures at 84.20. At expiry, the FBIL reference rate is 83.80. What is the profit/loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: A short futures seller profits when the settlement price is lower than the contracted price. P&L = (Entry - Final) x Lot x Lots = (84.20 - 83.80) x 1000 x 10 = 0.40 x 10000 = Rs. 4,000 profit. USDINR lot size is 1000 USD and final settlement uses the FBIL reference rate. The Trap: For short positions, profit equals entry price minus settlement price, not the other way around. Note: The final settlement value is based on the FBIL reference rate rather than the last traded futures price.
